questions.previousText: Police should need a court warrant to search someone’s home without their consent, except when there is an immediate threat to someone’s safety.
questions.text: Adults should be allowed to own firearms for personal defence, subject to checks for a history of violence.
questions.reason: Move existing firearm self-defence rights into all quiz lengths; keep wording, response and direction unchanged.

questions.previousText: The government should be able to require adults to carry identification and show it to police on request, even when they are not suspected of an offence.
questions.text: The government should be able to make vaccination against a serious infectious disease a condition for adults to enter shared public spaces during an outbreak.
questions.reason: Measure a bounded infectious-disease safety restriction rather than compulsory identification; distinguish protecting others from personal paternalism in item 05.

questions.previousText: Authorities should be able to restrict a person’s movements on security grounds without giving that person a prompt opportunity to challenge the restriction in an independent court.
questions.text: Authorities should be able to place people assessed by a court as posing a serious risk of violence under preventive movement restrictions, with regular judicial review.
questions.reason: Measure acceptance of preventive security controls with meaningful review; item 16 separately covers denial of review.

questions.previousText: Police should be allowed to search people and their belongings without individual grounds to suspect an offence, outside an immediate emergency.
questions.text: Police should be allowed to stop and search people without individual suspicion in a designated area for a limited period when there is credible evidence of a serious threat to public safety.
questions.reason: Measure temporary geographically limited policing powers justified by a credible threat, distinct from ordinary individual searches.

questions.previousText: People should need government permission before forming a peaceful civic association.
questions.text: The government should be able to prohibit public expression that incites hatred against people because of their race or religion, even when it does not directly threaten violence.
questions.reason: Measure nonviolent racial/religious incitement restrictions, distinct from offensive institutional criticism in item 01 and moral-content policy in item 09.
